I've now read the project thoroughly (all 180 Python files, ~48k LOC, schema, core services, data layer, docs). Here's what I found before proposing the rewrite.

## What this project actually is

**BOP Nutraceuticals ERP** — a double-entry accounting + manufacturing ERP for a pharma/nutraceutical business (the data exports say the real system is "PharmaPro"). 

- **Stack today:** Python 3.9 + **PySide6 (Qt6 desktop GUI)** + **SQLite Cloud** (hosted, network DB), ~35k LOC of app code.
- **Layers:** `models` (dataclasses) → `repositories` (raw SQL) → `services` (business logic) → `controllers` → `views` (Qt widgets).
- **Domain modules:** Chart of Accounts, journal/double-entry engine, parties (customer/supplier), inventory + batch tracking, sales & purchase invoices, payments/receipts, manufacturing (BOM + production orders), expenses, banking/cheques, assets, reports (Trial Balance, P&L, Balance Sheet, Party Ledger, Cash Book), PDF/Excel/CSV export, auth (PBKDF2) with roles/permissions, audit log, settings, backups.
- **Schema:** ~30 tables, money stored as `REAL` **floats**, soft-deletes, multi-company/multi-warehouse columns already present.

## Why the current language is a poor fit

1. **Money as floats** — the schema stores `REAL`, the services manually `round(x, 2)`. Your own `DATA_FLOW_ANALYSIS.md` flags this ("Use Decimal for money"). This is the #1 correctness risk in an accounting system.
2. **Desktop Qt in Python** — 12k lines of view code, sluggish data-heavy tables, and a custom network connection pool with retry/savepoint hacks to paper over running a *hosted* DB from a desktop client.
3. **`dict`-passing everywhere** — no compile-time guarantees; `from_row`/`to_dict` boilerplate that a typed language removes.
4. **Tests need a live cloud DB** (`cloud` marker) — hard to verify.

## My recommendation

Given this is a **multi-user networked business system** and needs **exact decimal money + strong typing**, the most appropriate target is a **TypeScript full-stack app** (typed end-to-end, real `DECIMAL` in Postgres, browser-based reporting/printing, no installs for users). It's also the only non-Python toolchain installed here (`node v22`), so I can actually build and verify it.

**Question:** Which database should the rebuilt system target?
_Answer:_ Keep SQLite Cloud (existing hosted DB)

**Question:** How should we sequence the rebuild? (The full app is ~35k LOC — it will take multiple passes.)
_Answer:_ Vertical slice first: accounting core + sales, end-to-end

text: |
    Node.js Quick Start Guide
    In this quickstart, we will show you how to get started with SQLite Cloud and Node.js by building a simple web server that connects to and reads from a SQLite Cloud database, then serves that data to the client.
    Set up a SQLite Cloud account
    If you haven’t already, sign up for a SQLite Cloud account and create a new project.
    In this guide, we will use the sample datasets that come pre-loaded with SQLite Cloud.

    Navigate to your target directory and run the following command to initialize your Node.js app and install the necessary depedencies:

    const connectionString = process.env.SQLITECLOUD_CONNECTION_STRING
    const app = express();
    app.get("/albums", async (req, res) => {
    let db = null;
    try {
    db = new Database(connectionString)
    const result = await db.sql(`
    USE DATABASE chinook.sqlite;
    SELECT albums.AlbumId as id, albums.Title as title, artists.name as artist
    FROM albums
    INNER JOIN artists
    WHERE artists.ArtistId = albums.ArtistId
    LIMIT 20;`);
    res.json(result);
    } catch (error) {
    res.status(500).json({ error: error.message });
    } finally {
    db?.close();
    }
    });
    app.listen(3000, () => {
    console.log("Server running on port 3000");
    });
    Run your app

    View your web server response
    Open your browser and navigate to http://localhost:3000/albums to see your app in action.

    # @sqlitecloud/drivers
    [![npm package][npm-img]][npm-url]
    [![Test][test-img]][test-url]
    [![Downloads][downloads-img]][downloads-url]
    [![Issues][issues-img]][issues-url]

    ## Install
    ### Web / Node.js / Next.js
    ```bash
    npm install @sqlitecloud/drivers
    ```
    No additional dependencies required - the package works out of the box.
    ### React Native / Expo
    When using this package in React Native or Expo projects, you must install the required peer dependencies. These dependencies are optional and not installed automatically to avoid polluting web and Node.js projects with unnecessary packages.
    ```bash
    npm install @sqlitecloud/drivers react-native-tcp-socket react-native-quick-base64 @craftzdog/react-native-buffer react-native-url-polyfill
    ```
    If you forget to install these dependencies, the package will throw clear error messages indicating which dependency is missing and how to install it.
    React Native run iOS
    ```bash
    cd ios && pod install && cd .. && npm run ios
    ```
    React Native run Android (without ./ in Windows)
    ```bash
    cd android && ./gradlew clean build && cd .. && npm run android
    ```
    Expo run iOS
    ```bash
    npx expo prebuild && npx expo run:ios
    ```
    Expo run Android
    ```bash
    npx expo prebuild && npx expo run:android
    ```
    ## Usage
    ```ts
    import { Database } from '@sqlitecloud/drivers'
    let database = new Database('sqlitecloud://user:password@xxx.sqlite.cloud:8860/chinook.sqlite')
    // or use sqlitecloud://xxx.sqlite.cloud:8860?apikey=xxxxxxx
    let name = 'Breaking The Rules'
    let results = await database.sql('SELECT * FROM tracks WHERE name = ?', name)
    // => returns [{ AlbumId: 1, Name: 'Breaking The Rules', Composer: 'Angus Young... }]
    ```
    Use [Database.sql](https://sqlitecloud.github.io/sqlitecloud-js/classes/Database.html#sql) to execute prepared statements or plain SQL queries asynchronously. This method returns an array of rows for SELECT queries and supports the standard syntax for UPDATE, INSERT, and DELETE.
    We aim for full compatibility with the established [sqlite3 API](https://www.npmjs.com/package/sqlite3), with the primary distinction being that our driver connects to SQLiteCloud databases. This allows you to migrate your [SQLite to the cloud](https://sqlitecloud.io) while continuing to use your existing codebase.
    The package is developed entirely in TypeScript and is fully compatible with JavaScript. It doesn't require any native libraries. This makes it a straightforward and effective tool for managing cloud-based databases in a familiar SQLite environment.
    ## Examples
    Check out all the supported platforms with related examples [here](https://github.com/sqlitecloud/sqlitecloud-js/tree/main/examples)!
    ## More

      """
      Password hashing utilities.
      
      Uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with a random per-user salt (stdlib `hashlib`,
      no extra dependency required). This is the single place password
      hashing happens, so upgrading the algorithm later (e.g. to argon2)
      only requires changing this module.
      """
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      import hashlib
      import hmac
      import os
      
      _ITERATIONS = 200_000
      _ALGO = "sha256"
      
      
      def hash_password(plain_password: str, salt: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, str]:
          """
          Returns (salt_hex, hash_hex). If salt is not provided, a new random
          16-byte salt is generated (used when creating/resetting a password).
          """
          salt_bytes = bytes.fromhex(salt) if salt else os.urandom(16)
          digest = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac(
              _ALGO, plain_password.encode("utf-8"), salt_bytes, _ITERATIONS
          )
          return salt_bytes.hex(), digest.hex()
      
      
      def verify_password(plain_password: str, salt_hex: str, expected_hash_hex: str) -> bool:
          _, computed_hash = hash_password(plain_password, salt_hex)
          return hmac.compare_digest(computed_hash, expected_hash_hex)

      """
      Authentication service.
      
      Only one accountant uses the system today, but this is written as a
      real username/password login against the `users` table (not a stub),
      so Admin/Manager/Storekeeper/Production Manager roles and per-user
      permissions (already modeled in roles/permissions/role_permissions)
      can be turned on later without changing this module's public API.
      """
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      from database.connection import DatabaseConnection, get_db
      from models.user import User
      from repositories.user_repository import RoleRepository, UserRepository
      from utils.exceptions import AuthenticationError, ValidationError
      from utils.logger import get_logger
      from utils.security import hash_password, verify_password
      
      logger = get_logger(__name__)
      
      
      class AuthService:
          def __init__(self, db: DatabaseConnection | None = None):
              self.db = db or get_db()
              self.user_repo = UserRepository(self.db)
              self.role_repo = RoleRepository(self.db)
              self._current_user: User | None = None
      
          @property
          def current_user(self) -> User | None:
              return self._current_user
      
          def login(self, username: str, password: str) -> User:
              row = self.user_repo.find_by_username(username.strip())
              if row is None or not row["is_active"]:
                  logger.warning("Failed login attempt for username=%s", username)
                  raise AuthenticationError("Invalid username or password.")
      
              if not verify_password(password, row["password_salt"], row["password_hash"]):
                  logger.warning("Failed login attempt for username=%s", username)
                  raise AuthenticationError("Invalid username or password.")
              
              self.user_repo.update_last_login(row["id"])
              user = User.from_row(row)
              self._current_user = user
              logger.info("User '%s' logged in (role=%s)", user.username, user.role_name)
              return user
      
          def logout(self) -> None:
              if self._current_user:
                  logger.info("User '%s' logged out", self._current_user.username)
              self._current_user = None
      
          def change_password(self, user_id: int, old_password: str, new_password: str) -> None:
              row = self.user_repo.get_by_id(user_id)
              if not verify_password(old_password, row["password_salt"], row["password_hash"]):
                  raise AuthenticationError("Current password is incorrect.")
              if len(new_password) < 6:
                  raise ValidationError("New password must be at least 6 characters.")
              salt, pwd_hash = hash_password(new_password)
              self.user_repo.update_password(user_id, salt, pwd_hash)
              logger.info("Password changed for user id=%s", user_id)
      
          # --- user administration (admin UI) ---------------------------------------
      
          def list_users(self) -> list[dict]:
              """All users joined with their role names."""
              return self.user_repo.find_all_with_roles()
      
          def get_user(self, user_id: int) -> dict | None:
              """Single user row (with role name) or None."""
              return self.user_repo.find_with_role_by_id(user_id)
      
          def create_user(self, username: str, full_name: str, password: str,
                          role_name: str, email: str | None = None,
                          is_active: bool = True) -> None:
              """Create a user. Raises ValidationError on bad input."""
              if not username or not username.strip():
                  raise ValidationError("Username is required.")
              if not password:
                  raise ValidationError("Password is required.")
              if len(password) < 6:
                  raise ValidationError("Password must be at least 6 characters.")
              if self.user_repo.find_by_username(username):
                  raise ValidationError(f"Username '{username}' already exists.")
              role = self.role_repo.find_by_name(role_name)
              if not role:
                  raise ValidationError(f"Role '{role_name}' not found.")
              salt, pwd_hash = hash_password(password)
              self.user_repo.insert({
                  "username": username,
                  "full_name": full_name,
                  "email": email,
                  "password_hash": pwd_hash,
                  "password_salt": salt,
                  "role_id": role["id"],
                  "is_active": 1 if is_active else 0,
              })
              logger.info("Created user: %s (%s)", username, role_name)
      
          def update_user(self, user_id: int, full_name: str, email: str | None,
                          role_name: str, is_active: bool,
                          password: str | None = None) -> None:
              """Update profile/role/status, optionally setting a new password."""
              role = self.role_repo.find_by_name(role_name)
              if not role:
                  raise ValidationError(f"Role '{role_name}' not found.")
              data: dict = {
                  "full_name": full_name,
                  "email": email,
                  "role_id": role["id"],
                  "is_active": 1 if is_active else 0,
              }
              if password:
                  if len(password) < 6:
                      raise ValidationError("Password must be at least 6 characters.")
                  salt, pwd_hash = hash_password(password)
                  data["password_hash"] = pwd_hash
                  data["password_salt"] = salt
              self.user_repo.update(user_id, data)
              logger.info("Updated user id=%s", user_id)
      
          def reset_password(self, user_id: int, new_password: str) -> None:
              """Set a new password without knowing the old one (admin action)."""
              if not new_password:
                  raise ValidationError("Password is required.")
              if len(new_password) < 6:
                  raise ValidationError("Password must be at least 6 characters.")
              salt, pwd_hash = hash_password(new_password)
              self.user_repo.update_password(user_id, salt, pwd_hash)
              logger.info("Reset password for user id=%s", user_id)

> Architecture decision (final):
> - Monorepo at `web/` using npm workspaces.
> - `web/server`: Express + TypeScript. Uses `@sqlitecloud/drivers` for prod, `node:sqlite` for local/test.
> - `web/client`: React + Vite + TypeScript.
> - `web/shared`: shared domain types (enums, DTOs) — a workspace package `@erp/shared`.

> 1. **Money**: `Money.ts` using decimal.js; helpers for parse/sum/round; serialization to number.
> 2. **Domain**: enums (AccountType, PartyType, VoucherType, PaymentMethod, DocumentStatus), types.
> 3. **DB**: `SqlDatabase` interface + `SqliteCloudDatabase` + `LocalSqliteDatabase`; schema DDL (reuse existing schema.ts) for local tests/seeding; transaction support.
> 4. **Repositories**: Account, Party, Item, StockBatch, Journal, SalesInvoice, User.
> 5. **Services**: `AccountingService` (postJournalEntry, getTrialBalance, getAccountBalance, nextVoucherNumber), `SalesInvoiceService` (create with stock deduction + JE, list, get), `ReportService` (trial balance, P&L maybe), `AuthService` (PBKDF2).
> 6. **HTTP API** (Express): `/api/auth/login`, `/api/accounts`, `/api/parties`, `/api/items`, `/api/sales-invoices` (GET list, GET :id, POST), `/api/reports/trial-balance`.
> 7. **Client** (React + Vite): Login page, layout/nav, Sales Invoices list + create (line items, totals), Chart of Accounts, Trial Balance.
> 8. **Tests** (vitest): money, accounting (balance validation, voucher numbering), sales totals + JE correctness + stock. Plus an integration test on local sqlite through the service layer.
> 9. **Verification**: `tsc --noEmit`, `vitest run`, start server, curl smoke test against local sqlite seeded, and optionally test the SQLite Cloud adapter connection (read-only) if reachable.

> _Reasoning_
> `Database` uses a **single** connection (`this.connection`), not really a pool — `createConnection` creates one connection and `enqueueCommand` sends on it. So `Database` is effectively a single-connection client with a serialized operations queue. That means **BEGIN/COMMIT across multiple `sql()` calls WILL work**, because all commands go to the same connection and are serialized via the operations queue.
> 
> That's great news — transactions are safe with the `Database` class as long as I serialize them. Since the operations queue serializes commands, and my transaction helper awaits each statement sequentially, BEGIN...COMMIT will hit the same connection.
> 
> But caution: concurrent requests sharing one `Database` instance could interleave. The queue serializes individual commands, but if two async flows interleave their BEGIN/COMMIT, transactions would mix. In the Python app, they used a pool with a transaction-held connection. Here, with a single connection, I need to ensure transaction mutual exclusion. I'll implement a simple async mutex around transactions in the production adapter so only one transaction runs at a time on the shared connection. That's correct and simple (SQLite is single-writer anyway).
> 
> For local tests (node:sqlite DatabaseSync), transactions are synchronous and simple.
> 
> OK. Now I have enough to design the DB abstraction.
>

> ```ts
> export interface SqlDatabase {
>   all<T = Row>(sql: string, params?: SqlParam[]): Promise<T[]>;
>   get<T = Row>(sql: string, params?: SqlParam[]): Promise<T | undefined>;
>   run(sql: string, params?: SqlParam[]): Promise<{ changes: number; lastInsertRowid: number }>;
>   exec(sql: string): Promise<void>;      // multiple statements, no params (DDL)
>   transaction<T>(fn: (tx: SqlDatabase) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
>   close(): Promise<void>;
> }
> ```
> 
> For SQLite Cloud:
> - `run`: use `db.sql({query, parameters})`? The `sql` accepts a `SQLiteCloudCommand` {query, parameters} or template. For INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, returns metadata object? The README says "returns an object with metadata in case of insert, update, delete". The `processContext` maps ARRAY_TYPE_SQLITE_EXEC to {lastID, changes,...}.       (see database/migrations/migrator.py -> SYSTEM_ACCOUNTS).
      
      Other services (sales, purchases, banking, manufacturing, expenses)
      resolve the account they need to post against by *code*, never by a
      hardcoded numeric id, since ids can differ between environments while
      codes are guaranteed by the seed data.

      from __future__ import annotations
      
      from database.connection import DatabaseConnection, get_db
      from repositories.account_repository import AccountRepository
      from utils.exceptions import ConfigurationError
      
      
      class SystemAccountCodes:
          CASH_IN_HAND = "1000"
          BANK_ACCOUNTS = "1010"
          ACCOUNTS_RECEIVABLE = "1100"
          INVENTORY_RAW_MATERIALS = "1200"
          INVENTORY_PACKING_MATERIALS = "1210"
          INVENTORY_FINISHED_GOODS = "1220"
          WITHHOLDING_TAX_RECEIVABLE = "1300"
          FIXED_ASSETS = "1500"
          HBL_INSTALMENT = "1501"
          MOTOR_CAR_INSTALMENT = "1502"
          AUTO_VEHICLES = "1503"
          FURNITURE_FIXTURES = "1504"
          CAR_SALE_PURCHASE = "1505"
          ACCOUNTS_PAYABLE = "2000"
          SALES_TAX_PAYABLE = "2100"
          WITHHOLDING_TAX_PAYABLE = "2200"
          OWNERS_EQUITY = "3000"
          RETAINED_EARNINGS = "3100"
          SALES_REVENUE = "4000"
          SALES_RETURNS = "4100"
          COST_OF_GOODS_SOLD = "5000"
          COST_OF_PACKING_MATERIALS = "5001"
          PURCHASE_RETURNS = "5100"
          MANUFACTURING_WASTAGE_EXPENSE = "5200"
          INVENTORY_LOSS_EXPENSE = "5300"
          GENERAL_ADMIN_EXPENSE = "6000"
          SELLING_EXPENSE = "6100"
      
      
      class SystemAccountResolver:
          """Resolves system account codes to their database id, with caching."""
      
          def __init__(self, db: DatabaseConnection | None = None, company_id: int = 1):
              self.db = db or get_db()
              self.company_id = company_id
              self._repo = AccountRepository(self.db)
              self._cache: dict[str, int] = {}
      
          def id_for(self, code: str) -> int:
              if code in self._cache:
                  return self._cache[code]
              account = self._repo.find_by_code(code, self.company_id)
              if account is None:
                  raise ConfigurationError(
                      f"Required system account '{code}' is missing. "
                      "Run database migrations to seed the default chart of accounts."
                  )
              self._cache[code] = account["id"]
              return account["id"]

          ("6000", "General & Administrative Expenses", "EXPENSE", None),
          ("6100", "Selling Expenses",            "EXPENSE",   None),
      ]
      
      # database/migrations/migrator.py
      
      # database/migrations/migrator.py
      
      DEFAULT_NUMBERING = [
              ("SALES_INVOICE", "SI-"),
              ("SALES_RETURN", "SR-"),
              ("PURCHASE_INVOICE", "PI-"),
              ("PURCHASE_RETURN", "PR-"),

      class Migrator:
          def __init__(self, db: DatabaseConnection):
              self._db = db
      
          def run(self) -> None:
              logger.info("Running schema migration...")
              with self._db.transaction():
                  for statement in ALL_STATEMENTS:
                      for sub_stmt in statement.strip().split(";"):
                          sub_stmt = sub_stmt.strip()
                          if sub_stmt:
                              self._db.execute(sub_stmt)
                  self._migrate_columns()
              logger.info("Schema migration complete.")
              self._seed_defaults()
      
          def _column_exists(self, table: str, column: str) -> bool:
              cols = [r["name"] for r in self._db.fetch_all(f"PRAGMA table_info({table})")]
              return column in cols
      
          def _migrate_columns(self) -> None:
              """Idempotently add columns added after the initial schema release."""
              if not self._column_exists("bill_of_materials", "is_ghost"):
                  self._db.execute(
                      "ALTER TABLE bill_of_materials ADD COLUMN is_ghost INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"
                  )
              if not self._column_exists("production_orders", "is_ghost"):
                  self._db.execute(
                      "ALTER TABLE production_orders ADD COLUMN is_ghost INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"
                  )
              # bank_account_id for invoices (added after initial release so it must

              # alter existing tables).
              for table in ("sales_invoices", "purchase_invoices"):
                  if not self._column_exists(table, "bank_account_id"):
                      self._db.execute(
                          f"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN bank_account_id INTEGER REFERENCES bank_accounts(id)"
                      )

                  self._seed_roles()

                  self._seed_default_user()
                  self._seed_default_settings()

          def _seed_company_and_warehouse(self) -> None:

              if not self._db.fetch_one("SELECT id FROM warehouses WHERE id = 1"):

      """Data access for the Chart of Accounts, including running-balance lookups."""
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      from repositories.base_repository import BaseRepository
      from utils.exceptions import DuplicateRecordError
      
      
      class AccountRepository(BaseRepository):
          table_name = "accounts"
      
          def find_by_code(self, account_code: str, company_id: int = 1) -> dict | None:
              cache_key = self._get_cache_key("find_by_code", account_code, company_id)
              cached = self._get_cached(cache_key)
              if cached is not None:
                  return cached
              
              result = self.db.fetch_one(
                  "SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE account_code = ? AND company_id = ?",
                  (account_code, company_id),
              )
              if result:
                  self._set_cached(cache_key, result)
              return result
      
          def code_exists(self, account_code: str, company_id: int = 1, exclude_id: int | None = None) -> bool:
              sql = "SELECT id FROM accounts WHERE account_code = ? AND company_id = ?"
              params: tuple = (account_code, company_id)
              if exclude_id is not None:
                  sql += " AND id != ?"
                  params += (exclude_id,)
              return self.db.fetch_one(sql, params) is not None
      
          def find_all_for_company(self, company_id: int = 1, active_only: bool = True) -> list[dict]:
              cache_key = self._get_cache_key("find_all_for_company", company_id, active_only)
              cached = self._get_cached(cache_key)
              if cached is not None:
                  return cached
              
              sql = "SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE company_id = ?"
              params: tuple = (company_id,)
              if active_only:
                  sql += " AND is_active = 1"
              sql += " ORDER BY account_code"
              result = self.db.fetch_all(sql, params)
              self._set_cached(cache_key, result)
              return result
      
          def find_by_type(self, account_type: str, company_id: int = 1) -> list[dict]:
              cache_key = self._get_cache_key("find_by_type", account_type, company_id)
              cached = self._get_cached(cache_key)
              if cached is not None:
                  return cached
              
              result = self.db.fetch_all(
                  "SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE account_type = ? AND company_id = ? "
                  "AND is_active = 1 ORDER BY account_code",
                  (account_type, company_id),
              )
              self._set_cached(cache_key, result)
              return result
      
          def find_children(self, parent_account_id: int) -> list[dict]:
              cache_key = self._get_cache_key("find_children", parent_account_id)
              cached = self._get_cached(cache_key)
              if cached is not None:
                  return cached
              
              result = self.db.fetch_all(
                  "SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE parent_account_id = ? ORDER BY account_code",
                  (parent_account_id,),
              )
              self._set_cached(cache_key, result)
              return result
      
          def get_current_balance(self, account_id: int) -> float:
              """
              Current balance = sum(debits) - sum(credits) for debit-normal
              accounts (ASSET/EXPENSE), or the mirror image for credit-normal
              accounts (LIABILITY/EQUITY/REVENUE), read directly from posted
              journal_entry_lines.
      
              Note: `accounts.opening_balance` is NOT added here. It is a
              display/reference field only -- AccountService posts every
              non-zero opening balance as its own OPENING journal entry (see
              AccountService._post_opening_balance) so it already flows
              through journal_entry_lines. Adding the column value on top
              would double-count it.
              """
              cache_key = self._get_cache_key("get_current_balance", account_id)
              cached = self._get_cached(cache_key)
              if cached is not None:
                  return cached
              
              account = self.get_by_id(account_id)
              totals = self.db.fetch_one(
                  """
                  SELECT COALESCE(SUM(debit), 0) AS total_debit,
                         COALESCE(SUM(credit), 0) AS total_credit
                  FROM journal_entry_lines jel
                  JOIN journal_entries je ON je.id = jel.journal_entry_id
                  WHERE jel.account_id = ? AND je.is_posted = 1
                  """,
                  (account_id,),
              )
              debit_total = totals["total_debit"]
              credit_total = totals["total_credit"]
      
              debit_normal = account["account_type"] in ("ASSET", "EXPENSE")
              if debit_normal:
                  balance = debit_total - credit_total
              else:
                  balance = credit_total - debit_total
              
              self._set_cached(cache_key, balance)
              return balance
      
          def insert_unique(self, data: dict) -> int:
              if self.code_exists(data["account_code"], data.get("company_id", 1)):
                  raise DuplicateRecordError(
                      f"Account code '{data['account_code']}' already exists."
                  )
              return self.insert(data)

  content: |
      """
      Data access for journal_entries / journal_entry_lines -- the physical
      ledger every other module (sales, purchases, banking, manufacturing,
      expenses) writes to via the AccountingService.
      """
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      from utils.logger import get_logger
      from utils.exceptions import DatabaseError
      from repositories.base_repository import BaseRepository
      
      logger = get_logger(__name__)
      
      
      class JournalRepository(BaseRepository):
          table_name = "journal_entries"
      
          def insert_entry(self, header: dict, lines: list[dict]) -> int:
              """
              Inserts one journal_entries row plus all its journal_entry_lines
              rows. Caller (AccountingService) is expected to wrap this in
              `db.transaction()` together with whatever else must commit
              atomically (e.g. the sales invoice row itself).
              
              Raises:
                  ValueError: If lines list is empty - every journal entry must have at least 2 lines
                  DatabaseError: If any account_id in lines doesn't exist in accounts table
              """
              logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() CALLED with header={header}, lines count={len(lines)}")
              logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() lines data: {lines}")
              
              if not lines:
                  logger.error("JournalRepository.insert_entry() lines list is EMPTY!")
                  raise ValueError("Cannot insert journal entry without lines. "
                                 "Every journal entry must have at least 2 lines.")
              
              # Validate all account_ids exist before inserting
              logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() STARTING validation of {len(lines)} account IDs")
              for order, line in enumerate(lines):
                  account_id = line.get("account_id")
                  logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() validating line {order}: account_id={account_id}, debit={line.get('debit')}, credit={line.get('credit')}")
                  
                  if account_id is None:
                      logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() line {order} has NO account_id!")
                      raise ValueError(f"Line {order} has no account_id")
                  
                  # Check if account exists - get FULL details
                  account_check = self.db.fetch_one("SELECT id, account_code, account_name, company_id, is_active, account_type FROM accounts WHERE id = ?", (account_id,))
                  logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() line {order}: account_check result={account_check}")
                  
                  if account_check is None:
                      logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() line {order}: account_id={account_id} DOES NOT EXIST in accounts table!")
                      
                      # Debug: List ALL accounts in the database
                      all_accounts = self.db.fetch_all("SELECT id, account_code, account_name, company_id, is_active FROM accounts ORDER BY id")
                      logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() ALL accounts in DB ({len(all_accounts)}):")
                      for acc in all_accounts:
                          logger.error(f"  Account: id={acc['id']}, code={acc['account_code']}, name={acc['account_name']}, company_id={acc['company_id']}, is_active={acc['is_active']}")
                      
                      raise DatabaseError(
                          f"Account ID {account_id} does not exist in the database. "
                          f"Line data: account_id={account_id}, debit={line.get('debit')}, credit={line.get('credit')}. "
                          f"Available account IDs: {[acc['id'] for acc in all_accounts]}"
                      )
                  logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() line {order}: account_id={account_id} EXISTS (code={account_check['account_code']}, name={account_check['account_name']}, company_id={account_check['company_id']}, is_active={account_check['is_active']})")
              
              logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() ALL account validations PASSED")
              
              # Build column names and placeholders for header insert
              columns = list(header.keys())
              values = [header[col] for col in columns]
              placeholders = ', '.join(['?'] * len(values))
              col_names = ', '.join(columns)
              
              # Insert header - get cursor to keep connection alive for last_insert_rowid()
              cursor = self.db.execute(
                  f"INSERT INTO journal_entries ({col_names}) VALUES ({placeholders})",
                  values,
                  return_cursor=True
              )
              
              # Get the last inserted ID from the same connection
              conn = cursor.connection
              entry_id = conn.execute("SELECT last_insert_rowid()").fetchone()[0]
              
              logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() inserted header with entry_id={entry_id}")
              
              if not entry_id or entry_id <= 0:
                  logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() FAILED to get valid entry_id, got {entry_id}")
                  raise DatabaseError("Failed to get generated journal entry ID")
              
              # DON'T commit or return connection here - caller (AccountingService) 
              # has wrapped this in db.transaction() and will handle commit/rollback
              # Just continue with inserting lines using the same transaction context
              
              for order, line in enumerate(lines):
                  line = dict(line)
                  line["journal_entry_id"] = entry_id
                  line.setdefault("line_order", order)
                  # Only include party_id if it's not None (to avoid FOREIGN KEY constraint failure)
                  if line.get("party_id") is None:
                      line.pop("party_id", None)
                  columns = list(line.keys())
                  placeholders = ", ".join("?" for _ in columns)
                  col_list = ", ".join(columns)
                  logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() inserting line {order}: account_id={line.get('account_id')}, debit={line.get('debit')}, credit={line.get('credit')}, columns={columns}, values={list(line.values())}")
                  try:
                      result = self.db.execute(
                          f"INSERT INTO journal_entry_lines ({col_list}) VALUES ({placeholders})",
                          tuple(line.values()),
                      )
                      logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() line {order} inserted successfully, result={result}")
                  except Exception as e:
                      logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() FAILED to insert line {order}: {e}")
                      logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() line data that failed: {line}")
                      
                      # Extra debug: check the account one more time right before insert
                      acc_id = line.get('account_id')
                      acc_check = self.db.fetch_one("SELECT id, account_code, account_name, company_id, is_active FROM accounts WHERE id = ?", (acc_id,))
                      logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() PRE-INSERT check for account_id={acc_id}: {acc_check}")
                      
                      # List all accounts again
                      all_accounts = self.db.fetch_all("SELECT id, account_code, account_name, company_id FROM accounts ORDER BY id")
                      logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() ALL accounts at time of failure ({len(all_accounts)}):")
                      for acc in all_accounts:
                          logger.error(f"  Account: id={acc['id']}, code={acc['account_code']}, name={acc['account_name']}, company_id={acc['company_id']}")
                      
                      raise
              logger.error(f"JournalRepository.insert_entry() ALL lines inserted successfully, returning entry_id={entry_id}")
              return entry_id
      
          def next_voucher_number(self, company_id: int, document_type: str) -> str:
              """Get next voucher number for the given document type.
              
              Uses atomic UPDATE ... RETURNING to prevent race conditions
              when multiple threads request numbers simultaneously.
              
              Args:
                  company_id: Company identifier
                  document_type: Type of document (e.g., 'SALES', 'PURCHASE')
                  
              Returns:
                  Formatted voucher number string
              """
              # Map voucher types to numbering sequence document types
              doc_type_mapping = {
                  'SALES': 'SALES_INVOICE',
                  'PURCHASE': 'PURCHASE_INVOICE',
                  'PAYMENT': 'PAYMENT',
                  'RECEIPT': 'RECEIPT',
                  'JOURNAL': 'JOURNAL_VOUCHER',
                  'OPENING': 'OPENING',
                  'CUSTOMER': 'CUSTOMER',
                  'SUPPLIER': 'SUPPLIER',
              }
              seq_doc_type = doc_type_mapping.get(document_type, document_type)
              
              # Atomic increment and fetch in one operation to prevent race conditions
              result = self.db.fetch_one(
                  """
                  INSERT INTO numbering_sequences (company_id, document_type, prefix, next_number, padding)
                  VALUES (?, ?, ?, 1, 5)
                  ON CONFLICT(company_id, document_type) DO UPDATE SET
                      next_number = next_number + 1
                  RETURNING prefix, next_number, padding
                  """,
                  (company_id, seq_doc_type, f"{seq_doc_type}-"),
              )
              
              prefix, next_number, padding = result["prefix"], result["next_number"], result["padding"]
              return f"{prefix}{str(next_number).zfill(padding)}"
          def next_voucher_numbers(self, company_id: int, document_type: str, count: int) -> list[str]:
              """Atomically reserve *count* sequential voucher numbers in one write."""
              doc_type_mapping = {
                  'SALES': 'SALES_INVOICE',
                  'PURCHASE': 'PURCHASE_INVOICE',
                  'PAYMENT': 'PAYMENT',
                  'RECEIPT': 'RECEIPT',
                  'JOURNAL': 'JOURNAL_VOUCHER',
                  'OPENING': 'OPENING',
                  'CUSTOMER': 'CUSTOMER',
                  'SUPPLIER': 'SUPPLIER',
                  'EXPENSE': 'EXPENSE',
              }
              seq_doc_type = doc_type_mapping.get(document_type, document_type)
              result = self.db.fetch_one(
                  """
                  INSERT INTO numbering_sequences (company_id, document_type, prefix, next_number, padding)
                  VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 5)
                  ON CONFLICT(company_id, document_type) DO UPDATE SET
                      next_number = next_number + ?
                  RETURNING prefix, next_number, padding
                  """,
                  (company_id, seq_doc_type, f"{seq_doc_type}-", count, count),
              )
              prefix = result["prefix"]
              end_number = result["next_number"]
              padding = result["padding"]
              return [
                  f"{prefix}{str(end_number - count + 1 + i).zfill(padding)}"
                  for i in range(count)
              ]
      
          def insert_entries_bulk(
              self, headers: list[dict], lines_per_entry: list[list[dict]]
          ) -> list[int]:
              """Insert multiple journal entries + lines in minimal round trips.
      
              Skips per-line account_id validation (caller must guarantee validity).
              Each entry gets a unique journal_entry_id assigned via last_insert_id
              offset calculation.  Must be called inside ``db.transaction()``.
              """
              if not headers:
                  return []
      
              # --- insert all headers in one executemany ---
              cols = list(headers[0].keys())
              placeholders = ", ".join("?" for _ in cols)
              col_list = ", ".join(cols)
              sql_h = f"INSERT INTO {self.table_name} ({col_list}) VALUES ({placeholders})"
              self.db.executemany(sql_h, [tuple(h[c] for c in cols) for h in headers])
      
              # figure out the range of generated IDs (assumes AUTOINCREMENT = sequential)
              last_id = self.db.last_insert_id()
              first_id = last_id - len(headers) + 1
              entry_ids = list(range(first_id, last_id + 1))
      
              # --- insert all lines in one executemany (flattened) ---
              all_lines: list[dict] = []
              for entry_id, lines in zip(entry_ids, lines_per_entry):
                  for order, line in enumerate(lines):
                      row = dict(line)
                      row["journal_entry_id"] = entry_id
                      row.setdefault("line_order", order)
                      if row.get("party_id") is None:
                          row.pop("party_id", None)
                      all_lines.append(row)
      
              if all_lines:
                  line_cols = list(dict.fromkeys(k for r in all_lines for k in r.keys()))
                  line_ph = ", ".join("?" for _ in line_cols)
                  line_cl = ", ".join(line_cols)
                  sql_l = f"INSERT INTO journal_entry_lines ({line_cl}) VALUES ({line_ph})"
                  self.db.executemany(sql_l, [tuple(r.get(c) for c in line_cols) for r in all_lines])
      
              return entry_ids
      
          def find_lines_for_entry(self, journal_entry_id: int) -> list[dict]:
              return self.db.fetch_all(
                  "SELECT jel.*, a.account_code, a.account_name FROM journal_entry_lines jel "
                  "JOIN accounts a ON a.id = jel.account_id "
                  "WHERE jel.journal_entry_id = ? ORDER BY jel.line_order",
                  (journal_entry_id,),
              )
      
          def find_entries_for_account(
              self, account_id: int, date_from: str | None = None, date_to: str | None = None
          ) -> list[dict]:
              sql = """
                  SELECT je.id, je.voucher_number, je.voucher_type, je.entry_date,
                         je.narration, jel.debit, jel.credit, jel.description
                  FROM journal_entry_lines jel
                  JOIN journal_entries je ON je.id = jel.journal_entry_id
                  WHERE jel.account_id = ? AND je.is_posted = 1
              """
              params: list = [account_id]
              if date_from:
                  sql += " AND je.entry_date >= ?"
                  params.append(date_from)
              if date_to:
                  sql += " AND je.entry_date <= ?"
                  params.append(date_to)
              sql += " ORDER BY je.entry_date, je.id"
              return self.db.fetch_all(sql, tuple(params))
      
          def find_by_source(self, source_table: str, source_id: int) -> dict | None:
              return self.db.fetch_one(
                  "SELECT * FROM journal_entries WHERE source_table = ? AND source_id = ?",
                  (source_table, source_id),
              )

> Transaction with serialize + BEGIN/COMMIT:
> ```ts
> async transaction<T>(fn: (tx: SqlDatabase) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
>   return this.serialize(async () => {
>     await this.execRaw("BEGIN");
>     try {
>       const result = await fn(this);
>       await this.execRaw("COMMIT");
>       return result;
>     } catch (e) {
>       try { await this.execRaw("ROLLBACK"); } catch {}
>       throw e;
>     }
>   });
> }
> ```
> Note: the serialize wrapper ensures the whole transaction body doesn't interleave with other calls. But fn calls this.all/this.run which themselves call serialize → those would deadlock because they'd be queued behind the currently-running transaction! That's a classic reentrancy bug.
> 
> I must avoid double-serialization. Options:
> - Don't serialize in all/get/run; rely on the driver's internal queue for individual commands, and serialize only transactions. But then a non-transaction command could slip into the middle of a transaction. However, since a transaction body awaits each command and the driver's queue serializes commands, an interleaved command from another request would break atomicity.
> - Better: track `inTx`. When inTx, all/get/run bypass the chain and call the driver directly (the driver's own queue still serializes commands, and since the transaction body executes synchronously in terms of awaiting, other requests' commands could still interleave...). Hmm.
> 
> Actually, the real fix: since Node is single-threaded and the HTTP handlers await, interleaving is possible only at await points. Between BEGIN and the next command there IS an await. So another request's DB call could enqueue between BEGIN and the first statement. To prevent that, I need to serialize at the request level. 
> 
> Simplest correct approach for this app: a global mutex for DB operations (every all/get/run/transaction acquires it). This serializes ALL DB access — acceptable for a small ERP over a single SQLite connection (SQLite is single-writer anyway; and the driver is one connection). This matches the Python app's effectively-serialized single connection model.
> 
> But holding a mutex for the entire transaction while the transaction's inner calls also try to acquire → deadlock. Need reentrancy: use a simple async mutex with an "owner" concept, or route inner calls through a flag.
> 
> Approach: Implement a mutex that supports reentrancy via an AsyncLocalStorage or a simple flag on the instance: `private held = false`. When entering transaction, acquire; set `this.locked = true`; inner calls check `if (this.heldByCurrentTx) run directly`. But detecting "current tx" without async context is unreliable.
> 
> Cleanest: Use `AsyncLocalStorage` to mark transaction context. Node has `node:async_hooks`. With ALS, inner calls can detect they're inside a transaction and bypass the mutex.
>

  "instructions": "Load .env files and expose typed configuration",
  "content": "/**\n * Central configuration, mirroring the Python project's config/app_config.py.\n *\n * Values come from web/.env or, as a fallback, the repository-root .env\n * (so the existing SQLITE_CLOUD_URL is picked up without duplication).\n * Nothing else in the codebase reads process.env directly.\n */\nimport fs from \"node:fs\";\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport { fileURLToPath } from \"node:url\";\n\nconst here = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)); // web/server/src\nconst serverRoot = path.resolve(here, \"..\"); // web/server\nconst webRoot = path.resolve(here, \"..\", \"..\"); // web\n\nfunction loadDotEnv(file: string): void {\n  if (!fs.existsSync(file)) return;\n  for (const raw of fs.readFileSync(file, \"utf8\").split(/\\r?\\n/)) {\n    const line = raw.trim();\n    if (!line || line.startsWith(\"#\") || !line.includes(\"=\")) continue;\n    const idx = line.indexOf(\"=\");\n    const key = line.slice(0, idx).trim();\n    let value = line.slice(idx + 1).trim();\n    if (\n      (value.startsWith('\"') && value.endsWith('\"')) ||\n      (value.startsWith(\"'\") && value.endsWith(\"'\"))\n    ) {\n      value = value.slice(1, -1);\n    }\n    if (process.env[key] === undefined) process.env[key] = value;\n  }\n}\n\n// web/.env wins, then the repository root .env fills in anything missing.\nloadDotEnv(path.join(webRoot, \".env\"));\nloadDotEnv(path.resolve(webRoot, \"..\", \".env\"));\n\nexport type DbEngine = \"local\" | \"sqlitecloud\";\n\nfunction readEngine(): DbEngine {\n  const raw = (process.env.ERP_DB_ENGINE ?? \"local\").toLowerCase();\n  return raw === \"sqlitecloud\" ? \"sqlitecloud\" : \"local\";\n}\n\nexport const env = {\n  dbEngine: readEngine(),\n  localDbPath: path.resolve(webRoot, process.env.ERP_LOCAL_DB ?? \"data/dev.sqlite\"),\n  sqliteCloudUrl: process.env.SQLITE_CLOUD_URL ?? \"\",\n  port: Number(process.env.PORT ?? 4000),\n  companyId: Number(process.env.ERP_COMPANY_ID ?? 1),\n  warehouseId: Number(process.env.ERP_WAREHOUSE_ID ?? 1),\n  currency: process.env.ERP_CURRENCY ?? \"PKR\",\n} as const;\n\nexport { serverRoot, webRoot };\n"
}

{
  "path": "web/server/src/domain/money.ts",
  "instructions": "Exact decimal money arithmetic helpers built on decimal.js",
  "content": "/**\n * Money handling.\n *\n * This is the single most important correction over the Python code base,\n * which stored money as IEEE-754 floats and manually rounded. All money\n * arithmetic here is done in exact decimal (decimal.js) and only converted\n * to a JS number at the database boundary, rounded half-up to 2 places.\n *\n * The database columns remain SQLite REAL so the new backend stays\n * byte-compatible with the existing Python app and its data.\n */\nimport Decimal from \"decimal.js\";\n\nDecimal.set({\n  precision: 34,\n  rounding: Decimal.ROUND_HALF_UP,\n  toExpNeg: -30,\n  toExpPos: 40,\n});\n\nexport const MONEY_DP = 2;\n\nexport type MoneyLike = Decimal | number | string | null | undefined;\n\n/** Coerce anything money-shaped into a Decimal without throwing on null. */\nexport function dec(value: MoneyLike): Decimal {\n  if (value === null || value === undefined) return new Decimal(0);\n  return value instanceof Decimal ? value : new Decimal(value);\n}\n\n/** Round to the storage scale (2 dp, half-up). Returns a Decimal. */\nexport function round2(value: MoneyLike): Decimal {\n  return dec(value).toDecimalPlaces(MONEY_DP, Decimal.ROUND_HALF_UP);\n}\n\n/** Value to persist into a REAL column. */\nexport function toStorage(value: MoneyLike): number {\n  return round2(value).toNumber();\n}\n\n/** Exact sum of many money values. */\nexport function sum(values: readonly MoneyLike[]): Decimal {\n  return values.reduce<Decimal>((acc, v) => acc.plus(dec(v)), new Decimal(0));\n}\n\n/** Multiply (quantity * price) then round to storage scale. */\nexport function multiply(a: MoneyLike, b: MoneyLike): Decimal {\n  return round2(dec(a).times(dec(b)));\n}\n\n/** Format as an amount with two decimals and thousands separators. */\nexport function formatAmount(value: MoneyLike): string {\n  return new Intl.NumberFormat(\"en-PK\", {\n    minimumFractionDigits: 2,\n    maximumFractionDigits: 2,\n  }).format(round2(value).toNumber());\n}\n\n/** Format with the configured currency symbol. */\nexport function formatMoney(value: MoneyLike, currency = \"PKR\"): string {\n  return new Intl.NumberFormat(\"en-PK\", {\n    style: \"currency\",\n    currency,\n    minimumFractionDigits: 2,\n    maximumFractionDigits: 2,\n  }).format(round2(value).toNumber());\n}\n\nexport { Decimal };\n"
}

  "content": "/**\n * SQLite Cloud adapter built on the official `@sqlitecloud/drivers` package.\n *\n * The driver opens a single serialized connection: `sql()` returns an array\n * of rows for SELECTs and a `{ lastID, changes }` context object for writes.\n * Because every command goes to the same connection, BEGIN/COMMIT works, but\n * we still guard the whole transaction with an async lock so a concurrent\n * request cannot interleave statements into the middle of it.\n *\n * `AsyncLocalStorage` makes the lock re-entrant: statements issued *inside* a\n * transaction body bypass the lock (they already hold it), while nested\n * `transaction()` calls simply join the outer one.\n */\nimport { AsyncLocalStorage } from \"node:async_hooks\";\nimport { Database } from \"@sqlitecloud/drivers\";\nimport { DatabaseError } from \"../domain/errors.js\";\nimport type { Row, RunResult, SqlDatabase, SqlValue } from \"./types.js\";\n\nconst txContext = new AsyncLocalStorage<boolean>();\n\ninterface WriteContext {\n  changes?: number;\n  lastID?: number | bigint;\n}\n\nexport class SqliteCloudDatabase implements SqlDatabase {\n  private readonly db: Database;\n  private chain: Promise<unknown> = Promise.resolve();\n\n  constructor(connectionString: string) {\n    if (!connectionString) {\n      throw new DatabaseError(\"SQLITE_CLOUD_URL is not set.\");\n    }\n    this.db = new Database(connectionString);\n  }\n\n  /** Serialize operations unless we are already inside the held transaction. */\n  private schedule<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {\n    if (txContext.getStore()) return fn();\n    const run = this.chain.then(fn, fn);\n    this.chain = run.then(\n      () => undefined,\n      () => undefined,\n    );\n    return run;\n  }\n\n  private async query(sql: string, params: readonly SqlValue[]): Promise<unknown> {\n    try {\n      return await this.db.sql({ query: sql, parameters: [...params] });\n    } catch (err) {\n      throw new DatabaseError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err), { sql });\n    }\n  }\n\n  async all<T = Row>(sql: string, params: readonly SqlValue[] = []): Promise<T[]> {\n    return this.schedule(async () => {\n      const result = await this.query(sql, params);\n      return Array.isArray(result) ? (result as T[]) : [];\n    });\n  }\n\n  async get<T = Row>(sql: string, params: readonly SqlValue[] = []): Promise<T | undefined> {\n    const rows = await this.all<T>(sql, params);\n    return rows[0];\n  }\n\n  async run(sql: string, params: readonly SqlValue[] = []): Promise<RunResult> {\n    return this.schedule(async () => {\n      const result = await this.query(sql, params);\n      if (result && typeof result === \"object\" && !Array.isArray(result)) {\n        const ctx = result as WriteContext;\n        if (\"changes\" in ctx || \"lastID\" in ctx) {\n          return {\n            changes: Number(ctx.changes ?? 0),\n            lastInsertRowid: Number(ctx.lastID ?? 0),\n          };\n        }\n      }\n      // Some statements (e.g. plain INSERT) may come back without a context;\n      // fall back to querying the rowid on the same connection.\n      const row = await this.rawGet<{ id: number }>(\"SELECT last_insert_rowid() AS id\");\n      return { changes: 0, lastInsertRowid: Number(row?.id ?? 0) };\n    });\n  }\n\n  private async rawGet<T>(sql: string): Promise<T | undefined> {\n    const result = await this.query(sql, []);\n    if (Array.isArray(result)) return result[0] as T | undefined;\n    return undefined;\n  }\n\n  async exec(sql: string): Promise<void> {\n    await this.schedule(\n      () =>\n        new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {\n          try {\n            this.db.exec(sql, (err) => (err ? reject(err) : resolve()));\n          } catch (err) {\n            reject(err);\n          }\n        }),\n    );\n  }\n\n  async transaction<T>(fn: (tx: SqlDatabase) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {\n    // Join an in-progress transaction rather than opening a nested one.\n    if (txContext.getStore()) {\n      return fn(this);\n    }\n    return this.schedule(async () => {\n      await this.execDirect(\"BEGIN\");\n      try {\n        const result = await txContext.run(true, () => fn(this));\n        await this.execDirect(\"COMMIT\");\n        return result;\n      } catch (err) {\n        try {\n          await this.execDirect(\"ROLLBACK\");\n        } catch {\n          // rollback best-effort; surface the original error\n        }\n        throw err;\n      }\n    });\n  }\n\n  /** Exec without touching the lock (used from inside a held transaction). */\n  private execDirect(sql: string): Promise<void> {\n    return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {\n      try {\n        this.db.exec(sql, (err) => (err ? reject(err) : resolve()));\n      } catch (err) {\n        reject(err);\n      }\n    });\n  }\n\n  async close(): Promise<void> {\n    await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {\n      try {\n        this.db.close(() => resolve());\n      } catch {\n        resolve();\n      }\n    });\n  }\n}\n"
}

{
  "path": "web/server/src/repositories/base.ts",
  "instructions": "Shared insert helper used by all repositories",
  "content": "import type { SqlDatabase, SqlValue } from \"../db/types.js\";\n\nexport type InsertData = Record<string, SqlValue>;\n\n/**\n * Insert one row and return its new id. Falls back to `last_insert_rowid()`\n * when the driver does not surface it in the write context (some SQLite Cloud\n * responses omit it for plain INSERTs).\n */\nexport async function insertRow(\n  db: SqlDatabase,\n  table: string,\n  data: InsertData,\n): Promise<number> {\n  const cols = Object.keys(data);\n  if (cols.length === 0) {\n    throw new Error(`No columns supplied for insert into ${table}`);\n  }\n  const placeholders = cols.map(() => \"?\").join(\", \");\n  const result = await db.run(\n    `INSERT INTO ${table} (${cols.join(\", \")}) VALUES (${placeholders})`,\n    cols.map((c) => data[c] ?? null),\n  );\n  if (result.lastInsertRowid > 0) return result.lastInsertRowid;\n  const row = await db.get<{ id: number }>(\"SELECT last_insert_rowid() AS id\");\n  return Number(row?.id ?? 0);\n}\n"
}

  "path": "web/server/src/repositories/accountRepository.ts",
  "instructions": "Data access for the chart of accounts and running balances",
  "content": "import type { SqlDatabase } from \"../db/types.js\";\nimport type { AccountType } from \"../domain/enums.js\";\nimport { isDebitNormal } from \"../domain/enums.js\";\nimport { NotFoundError } from \"../domain/errors.js\";\nimport { round2 } from \"../domain/money.js\";\nimport { insertRow, type InsertData } from \"./base.js\";\n\nexport interface AccountRow {\n  id: number;\n  company_id: number;\n  account_code: string;\n  account_name: string;\n  parent_account_id: number | null;\n  account_type: AccountType;\n  account_subtype: string | null;\n  opening_balance: number;\n  is_system_account: number;\n  is_active: number;\n  created_at: string;\n}\n\nexport class AccountRepository {\n  constructor(private readonly db: SqlDatabase) {}\n\n  async findByCode(code: string, companyId = 1): Promise<AccountRow | undefined> {\n    return this.db.get<AccountRow>(\n      \"SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE account_code = ? AND company_id = ?\",\n      [code, companyId],\n    );\n  }\n\n  async requireByCode(code: string, companyId = 1): Promise<AccountRow> {\n    const account = await this.findByCode(code, companyId);\n    if (!account) {\n      throw new NotFoundError(`Account '${code}' not found for company ${companyId}.`);\n    }\n    return account;\n  }\n\n  async findById(id: number): Promise<AccountRow | undefined> {\n    return this.db.get<AccountRow>(\"SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id = ?\", [id]);\n  }\n\n  async listForCompany(companyId = 1, activeOnly = true): Promise<AccountRow[]> {\n    const sql =\n      \"SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE company_id = ?\" +\n      (activeOnly ? \" AND is_active = 1\" : \"\") +\n      \" ORDER BY account_code\";\n    return this.db.all<AccountRow>(sql, [companyId]);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Current balance from posted journal lines only. `opening_balance` is a\n   * display field and is deliberately not added (the Python app posts every\n   * opening balance as its own OPENING journal entry, so adding it would\n   * double-count).\n   */\n  async getCurrentBalance(accountId: number): Promise<number> {\n    const account = await this.findById(accountId);\n    if (!account) throw new NotFoundError(`Account ${accountId} not found.`);\n    const totals = await this.db.get<{ total_debit: number; total_credit: number }>(\n      `SELECT COALESCE(SUM(debit), 0) AS total_debit,\n              COALESCE(SUM(credit), 0) AS total_credit\n       FROM journal_entry_lines jel\n       JOIN journal_entries je ON je.id = jel.journal_entry_id\n       WHERE jel.account_id = ? AND je.is_posted = 1`,\n      [accountId],\n    );\n    const debit = Number(totals?.total_debit ?? 0);\n    const credit = Number(totals?.total_credit ?? 0);\n    const balance = isDebitNormal(account.account_type) ? debit - credit : credit - debit;\n    return round2(balance).toNumber();\n  }\n\n  async codeExists(code: string, companyId = 1): Promise<boolean> {\n    const row = await this.db.get<{ id: number }>(\n      \"SELECT id FROM accounts WHERE account_code = ? AND company_id = ?\",\n      [code, companyId],\n    );\n    return row !== undefined;\n  }\n\n  async insert(data: InsertData): Promise<number> {\n    return insertRow(this.db, \"accounts\", data);\n  }\n}\n"
}

Mirrors accounting/system_accounts.py: services must\n * never hardcode numeric ids, since they differ between environments.\n */\nexport class SystemAccountResolver {\n  private readonly cache = new Map<string, number>();\n\n  constructor(\n    private readonly db: SqlDatabase,\n    private readonly companyId = 1,\n  ) {}\n\n  async idFor(code: string): Promise<number> {\n    const cached = this.cache.get(code);\n    if (cached !== undefined) return cached;\n    const row = await this.db.get<{ id: number }>(\n      \"SELECT id FROM accounts WHERE account_code = ? AND company_id = ?\",\n      [code, this.companyId],\n    );\n    if (!row) {\n      throw new ConfigurationError(\n        `Required system account '${code}' is missing. {
  "path": "web/server/src/repositories/journalRepository.ts",
  "instructions": "Data access for journal entries and lines, plus voucher numbering",
  "content": "import type { Row, SqlDatabase } from \"../db/types.js\";\nimport { AppError, ValidationError } from \"../domain/errors.js\";\nimport { insertRow, type InsertData } from \"./base.js\";\n\nexport interface JournalEntryHeader {\n  company_id: number;\n  voucher_number: string;\n  voucher_type: string;\n  entry_date: string;\n  reference_no?: string | null;\n  narration?: string | null;\n  source_table?: string | null;\n  source_id?: number | null;\n  is_posted?: number;\n  created_by?: number | null;\n}\n\nexport interface JournalLineRow {\n  account_id: number;\n  debit: number;\n  credit: number;\n  party_id?: number | null;\n  description?: string | null;\n}\n\n/** Maps a voucher type to the numbering_sequences document_type. */\nconst NUMBERING_DOC_TYPE: Record<string, string> = {\n  SALES: \"SALES_INVOICE\",\n  PURCHASE: \"PURCHASE_INVOICE\",\n  PAYMENT: \"PAYMENT\",\n  RECEIPT: \"RECEIPT\",\n  JOURNAL: \"JOURNAL_VOUCHER\",\n  OPENING: \"OPENING\",\n  CUSTOMER: \"CUSTOMER\",\n  SUPPLIER: \"SUPPLIER\",\n};\n\nexport class JournalRepository {\n  constructor(private readonly db: SqlDatabase) {}\n\n  /**\n   * Insert one journal entry header plus all of its lines. Must be called\n   * inside a transaction together with whatever else must commit atomically\n   * (e.g. the sales invoice row).\n   */\n  async insertEntry(header: JournalEntryHeader, lines: JournalLineRow[]): Promise<number> {\n    if (lines.length < 2) {\n      throw new ValidationError(\"A journal entry needs at least two lines.\");\n    }\n    const entryId = await insertRow(this.db, \"journal_entries\", {\n      ...header,\n      is_posted: header.is_posted ?? 1,\n    });\n    for (const [order, line] of lines.entries()) {\n      const row: InsertData = {\n        journal_entry_id: entryId,\n        account_id: line.account_id,\n        debit: line.debit,\n        credit: line.credit,\n        description: line.description ?? null,\n        line_order: order,\n      };\n      if (line.party_id !== undefined && line.party_id !== null) {\n        row.party_id = line.party_id;\n      }\n      await insertRow(this.db, \"journal_entry_lines\", row);\n    }\n    return entryId;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Atomically allocate the next voucher number, e.g. SI-00002. Uses an\n   * upsert-with-RETURNING identical to the Python implementation so numbers\n   * stay gap-free and consistent with the existing data.\n   */\n  async nextVoucherNumber(companyId: number, documentType: string): Promise<string> {\n    const seqDocType = NUMBERING_DOC_TYPE[documentType] ?? documentType;\n    const row = await this.db.get<{ prefix: string; next_number: number; padding: number }>(\n      `INSERT INTO numbering_sequences (company_id, document_type, prefix, next_number, padding)\n       VALUES (?, ?, ?, 1, 5)\n       ON CONFLICT(company_id, document_type) DO UPDATE SET\n           next_number = next_number + 1\n       RETURNING prefix, next_number, padding`,\n      [companyId, seqDocType, `${seqDocType}-`],\n    );\n    if (!row) {\n      throw new AppError(\"Failed to allocate a voucher number.\", \"NUMBERING_ERROR\", 500);\n    }\n    return `${row.prefix}${String(row.next_number).padStart(Number(row.padding), \"0\")}`;\n  }\n\n  async findLinesForEntry(journalEntryId: number): Promise<Row[]> {\n    return this.db.all<Row>(\n      `SELECT jel.*, a.account_code, a.account_name\n       FROM journal_entry_lines jel\n       JOIN accounts a ON a.id = jel.account_id\n       WHERE jel.journal_entry_id = ?\n       ORDER BY jel.line_order`,\n      [journalEntryId],\n    );\n  }\n\n  async findEntriesForAccount(\n    accountId: number,\n    dateFrom?: string,\n    dateTo?: string,\n  ): Promise<Row[]> {\n    let sql = `\n      SELECT je.id, je.voucher_number, je.voucher_type, je.entry_date,\n             je.narration, jel.debit, jel.credit, jel.description\n      FROM journal_entry_lines jel\n      JOIN journal_entries je ON je.id = jel.journal_entry_id\n      WHERE jel.account_id = ? AND je.is_posted = 1`;\n    const params: Array<string | number> = [accountId];\n    if (dateFrom) {\n      sql += \" AND je.entry_date >= ?\";\n      params.push(dateFrom);\n    }\n    if (dateTo) {\n      sql += \" AND je.entry_date <= ?\";\n      params.push(dateTo);\n    }\n    sql += \" ORDER BY je.entry_date, je.id\";\n    return this.db.all<Row>(sql, params);\n  }\n\n  async findBySource(sourceTable: string, sourceId: number): Promise<Row | undefined> {\n    return this.db.get<Row>(\n      \"SELECT * FROM journal_entries WHERE source_table = ? AND source_id = ?\",\n      [sourceTable, sourceId],\n    );\n  }\n}\n"
}

AND company_id = ?\",\n      [code, companyId],\n    );\n  }\n\n  async list(companyId = 1, activeOnly = true): Promise<ItemRow[]> {\n    return this.db.all<ItemRow>(\n      \"SELECT * FROM items WHERE company_id = ?\" +\n        (activeOnly ? \" AND is_active = 1\" : \"\") +\n        \" ORDER BY item_name\",\n      [companyId],\n    );\n  }\n\n  async insert(data: InsertData): Promise<number> {\n    return insertRow(this.db, \"items\", data);\n  }\n}\n"

  "path": "web/server/src/repositories/stockBatchRepository.ts",
  "instructions": "Data access for stock batches with FIFO lookup and quantity updates",
  "content": "import type { SqlDatabase } from \"../db/types.js\";\nimport { insertRow, type InsertData } from \"./base.js\";\n\nexport interface StockBatchRow {\n  id: number;\n  item_id: number;\n  warehouse_id: number;\n  batch_number: string;\n  manufacturing_date: string | null;\n  expiry_date: string | null;\n  purchase_price: number;\n  raw_unit_cost: number;\n  packing_unit_cost: number;\n  quantity_in_stock: number;\n  received_date: string;\n  is_active: number;\n  created_at: string;\n}\n\nexport class StockBatchRepository {\n  constructor(private readonly db: SqlDatabase) {}\n\n  /**\n   * Batches with available stock for an item, oldest first (FIFO). Batches\n   * with an expiry date sort before those without, so the soonest-to-expire\n   * stock leaves the warehouse first.\n   */\n  async listAvailableFifo(itemId: number, warehouseId: number): Promise<StockBatchRow[]> {\n    return this.db.all<StockBatchRow>(\n      `SELECT * FROM stock_batches\n       WHERE item_id = ? AND warehouse_id = ? AND is_active = 1 AND quantity_in_stock > 0\n       ORDER BY CASE WHEN expiry_date IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,\n                expiry_date, received_date, id`,\n      [itemId, warehouseId],\n    );\n  }\n\n  async getAvailableStock(itemId: number, warehouseId: number): Promise<number> {\n    const row = await this.db.get<{ qty: number | null }>(\n      `SELECT SUM(quantity_in_stock) AS qty FROM stock_batches\n       WHERE item_id = ? AND warehouse_id = ? AND is_active = 1`,\n      [itemId, warehouseId],\n    );\n    return Number(row?.qty ?? 0);\n  }\n\n  async findByItemAndWarehouse(\n    itemId: number,\n    warehouseId: number,\n  ): Promise<StockBatchRow | undefined> {\n    const batches = await this.listAvailableFifo(itemId, warehouseId);\n    return batches[0];\n  }\n\n  /** Apply a signed change to a batch's on-hand quantity. */\n  async adjustQuantity(batchId: number, delta: number): Promise<void> {\n    await this.db.run(\n      \"UPDATE stock_batches SET quantity_in_stock = quantity_in_stock + ? WHERE id = ?\",\n      [delta, batchId],\n    );\n  }\n\n  async insert(data: InsertData): Promise<number> {\n    return insertRow(this.db, \"stock_batches\", data);\n  }\n}\n"
}

AND invoice_number = ?\",\n      [companyId, invoiceNumber],\n    );\n    return row !== undefined;\n  }\n\n  async insertInvoice(data: InsertData): Promise<number> {\n    return insertRow(this.db, \"sales_invoices\", data);\n  }\n\n  async insertItem(data: InsertData): Promise<number> {\n    return insertRow(this.db, \"sales_invoice_items\", data);\n  }\n\n  async findById(id: number): Promise<SalesInvoiceRow | undefined> {\n    return this.db.get<SalesInvoiceRow>(\"SELECT * FROM sales_invoices WHERE id = ?\", [id]);\n  }\n\n  async findItems(invoiceId: number): Promise<Row[]> {\n    return this.db.all<Row>(\n      `SELECT sii.*, i.item_code, i.item_name, i.unit\n       FROM sales_invoice_items sii\n       JOIN items i ON i.id = sii.item_id\n       WHERE sii.invoice_id = ?\n       ORDER BY sii.id`,\n      [invoiceId],\n    );\n  }\n\n  async list(\n    companyId = 1,\n    opts: { limit?: number; offset?: number; search?: string; status?: DocumentStatus } = {},\n  ): Promise<SalesInvoiceListRow[]> {\n    let sql = `\n      SELECT si.*, p.name AS customer_name, p.code AS customer_code\n      FROM sales_invoices si\n      JOIN parties p ON p.id = si.customer_id\n      WHERE si.company_id = ?`;\n    const params: Array<string | number> = [companyId];\n    if (opts.status) {\n      sql += \" AND si.status = ?\";\n      params.push(opts.status);\n    }\n    if (opts.search) {\n      sql += \" AND (si.invoice_number LIKE ? OR p.name LIKE ?)\";\n      const like = `%${opts.search}%`;\n      params.push(like, like);\n    }\n    sql += \" ORDER BY si.invoice_date DESC, si.id DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?\";\n    params.push(opts.limit ?? 100, opts.offset ?? 0);\n    return this.db.all<SalesInvoiceListRow>(sql, params);\n  }\n\n  async count(companyId = 1): Promise<number> {\n    const row = await this.db.get<{ n: number }>(\n      \"SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM sales_invoices WHERE company_id = ?\",\n      [companyId],\n    );\n    return Number(row?.n ?? 0);\n  }\n}\n"

> import { pbkdf2Sync, randomBytes, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";
> const ITERATIONS = 200_000, KEYLEN = 32, DIGEST = "sha256";
> 
> export function hashPassword(plain: string, saltHex?: string): { salt: string; hash: string } {
>   const salt = saltHex ? Buffer.from(saltHex, "hex") : randomBytes(16);
>   const hash = pbkdf2Sync(plain, salt, ITERATIONS, KEYLEN, DIGEST);
>   return { salt: salt.toString("hex"), hash: hash.toString("hex") };
> }
> export function verifyPassword(plain: string, saltHex: string, expectedHashHex: string): boolean {
>   const { hash } = hashPassword(plain, saltHex);
>   const a = Buffer.from(hash, "hex");
>   const b = Buffer.from(expectedHashHex, "hex");
>   return a.length === b.length && timingSafeEqual(a, b);
> }
> ```

  "instructions": "Core double-entry accounting engine",
  "content": "/**\n * Core double-entry accounting engine.\n *\n * Every module that records money movement goes through postJournalEntry()\n * instead of touching journal_entries/journal_entry_lines directly, which\n * guarantees: entries are balanced before they are written, voucher numbers\n * are sequential per type, and every entry is traceable to its source\n * document. This mirrors services/accounting_service.py.\n */\nimport type { SqlDatabase } from \"../db/types.js\";\nimport { isDebitNormal, type AccountType, type VoucherType } from \"../domain/enums.js\";\nimport { UnbalancedJournalEntryError, ValidationError } from \"../domain/errors.js\";\nimport { Decimal, MoneyLike, round2, toStorage } from \"../domain/money.js\";\nimport { AccountRepository } from \"../repositories/accountRepository.js\";\nimport { JournalRepository, type JournalLineRow } from \"../repositories/journalRepository.js\";\n\nconst ROUNDING_TOLERANCE = \"0.01\";\n\nexport interface JournalLineInput {\n  accountId: number;\n  debit?: MoneyLike;\n  credit?: MoneyLike;\n  partyId?: number | null;\n  description?: string | null;\n}\n\nexport interface PostJournalEntryInput {\n  voucherType: VoucherType;\n  entryDate: string;\n  lines: readonly JournalLineInput[];\n  narration?: string | null;\n  referenceNo?: string | null;\n  sourceTable?: string | null;\n  sourceId?: number | null;\n  createdBy?: number | null;\n  companyId?: number;\n  voucherNumber?: string | null;\n}\n\nexport interface TrialBalanceRow {\n  accountId: number;\n  accountCode: string;\n  accountName: string;\n  accountType: AccountType;\n  debit: number;\n  credit: number;\n}\n\nexport class AccountingService {\n  private readonly journal: JournalRepository;\n  private readonly accounts: AccountRepository;\n\n  constructor(\n    private readonly db: SqlDatabase,\n    private readonly companyId = 1,\n  ) {\n    this.journal = new JournalRepository(db);\n    this.accounts = new AccountRepository(db);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Validate and write one balanced journal entry, returning its id. Callers\n   * that need atomicity must wrap this in db.transaction() together with the\n   * document it belongs to.\n   */\n  async postJournalEntry(input: PostJournalEntryInput): Promise<number> {\n    const lines = input.lines;\n    if (lines.length < 2) {\n      throw new ValidationError(\"A journal entry needs at least two lines.\");\n    }\n\n    const prepared = lines.map((line) => {\n      const debit = round2(line.debit ?? 0);\n      const credit = round2(line.credit ?? 0);\n      if (debit.isNegative() || credit.isNegative()) {\n        throw new ValidationError(\"Journal line amounts cannot be negative.\");\n      }\n      if (!debit.isZero() && !credit.isZero()) {\n        throw new ValidationError(\"A journal line cannot have both debit and credit.\");\n      }\n      return { line, debit, credit };\n    });\n\n    const totalDebit = prepared.reduce((acc, p) => acc.plus(p.debit), new Decimal(0));\n    const totalCredit = prepared.reduce((acc, p) => acc.plus(p.credit), new Decimal(0));\n    if (totalDebit.minus(totalCredit).abs().greaterThan(new Decimal(ROUNDING_TOLERANCE))) {\n      throw new UnbalancedJournalEntryError(\n        `Journal entry not balanced: debit=${totalDebit.toFixed(2)}, credit=${totalCredit.toFixed(2)}`,\n      );\n    }\n\n    const companyId = input.companyId ?? this.companyId;\n    const voucherNumber =\n      input.voucherNumber ??\n      (await this.journal.nextVoucherNumber(companyId, input.voucherType));\n\n    const rows: JournalLineRow[] = prepared.map(({ line, debit, credit }) => ({\n      account_id: line.accountId,\n      debit: toStorage(debit),\n      credit: toStorage(credit),\n      party_id: line.partyId ?? null,\n      description: line.description ?? null,\n    }));\n\n    return this.journal.insertEntry(\n      {\n        company_id: companyId,\n        voucher_number: voucherNumber,\n        voucher_type: input.voucherType,\n        entry_date: input.entryDate,\n        reference_no: input.referenceNo ?? null,\n        narration: input.narration ?? null,\n        source_table: input.sourceTable ?? null,\n        source_id: input.sourceId ?? null,\n        is_posted: 1,\n        created_by: input.createdBy ?? null,\n      },\n      rows,\n    );\n  }\n\n  async getJournalEntry(sourceTable: string, sourceId: number): Promise<Record<string, unknown> | null> {\n    const entry = await this.journal.findBySource(sourceTable, sourceId);\n    if (!entry) return null;\n    const lines = await this.journal.findLinesForEntry(Number(entry.id));\n    return { ...entry, lines };\n  }\n\n  async getAccountBalance(accountId: number): Promise<number> {\n    return this.accounts.getCurrentBalance(accountId);\n  }\n\n  /** One query returns every account with its posted debit/credit totals. */\n  async getTrialBalance(companyId = this.companyId): Promise<TrialBalanceRow[]> {\n    const rows = await this.db.all<{\n      id: number;\n      account_code: string;\n      account_name: string;\n      account_type: AccountType;\n      total_debit: number;\n      total_credit: number;\n    }>(\n      `SELECT a.id, a.account_code, a.account_name, a.account_type,\n              COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN je.is_posted = 1 THEN jel.debit ELSE 0 END), 0) AS total_debit,\n              COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN je.is_posted = 1 THEN jel.credit ELSE 0 END), 0) AS total_credit\n       FROM accounts a\n       LEFT JOIN journal_entry_lines jel ON jel.account_id = a.id\n       LEFT JOIN journal_entries je ON je.id = jel.journal_entry_id\n       WHERE a.company_id = ? AND a.is_active = 1\n       GROUP BY a.id, a.account_code, a.account_name, a.account_type\n       ORDER BY a.account_code`,\n      [companyId],\n    );\n\n    return rows.map((row) => {\n      const balance = new Decimal(row.total_debit).minus(new Decimal(row.total_credit));\n      const debitNormal = isDebitNormal(row.account_type);\n      const signed = debitNormal ? balance : balance.negated();\n      let debit = new Decimal(0);\n      let credit = new Decimal(0);\n      if (signed.greaterThanOrEqualTo(0)) {\n        debit = signed;\n      } else {\n        credit = signed.negated();\n      }\n      return {\n        accountId: row.id,\n        accountCode: row.account_code,\n        accountName: row.account_name,\n        accountType: row.account_type,\n        debit: toStorage(debit),\n        credit: toStorage(credit),\n      };\n    });\n  }\n}\n"
}
